type_note: user-visible: Nora can hold voice on several Discord servers, and two config keys change shape.
summary: Nora can hold voice on more than one Discord server at a time, and adding a server is one line of config — no new container, no new environment variable.
details: Until now a single audio-controller owned the one Discord voice connection and was bound to one server. A second server could have its speech recorded but nothing could ever join it. One controller process now holds a connection per server, and one wake gate serves all of them.

`[speech.tts] sidecar_endpoint` and `voice_guild_ids` are replaced by one key, `sidecars` — a list of `{ guild, endpoint }` entries. That list is the only place the set of voice servers is written down: a server is joinable exactly when it has an entry. Where each server's speech is RECORDED stays policy.toml's `voice = true`, and the two are independent on purpose.

The voice containers no longer carry any server id at all. Both used to take one from the environment, which put the same id in three files — policy.toml, config.toml and .env — with nothing saying which was authoritative. A server id is not a secret (it is in every Discord URL) so it never belonged in .env; the bot token stays there, and nothing else does.

The audio link between the two voice containers now says which server a connection carries, announced once when it connects. Without that the wake gate could not attribute what it heard, which is the only reason each server would otherwise need its own gate.
Restarting restores whatever connections were live, per server, from the controller's own state volume — it no longer needs to be told a channel to return to.
limitations: Each server still gets its own voice connection, its own state file and its own playback bookkeeping; sharing a process changes nothing about how one connection behaves. Discord's own limit is unchanged: one voice channel per server at a time, and a join to a second channel on the same server is refused as a conflict.
Asking the controller for status now requires naming a server. It refuses rather than defaulting, because defaulting would report one server's playback as another's.
A control request naming a server with no live connection is refused rather than creating one — only a join creates a connection, so the process cannot accumulate state for whatever a caller sends.

Not exercised live with two servers. Both sides of the audio link are covered by twin test suites that pin the wire format byte-for-byte, and the control plane is covered by the same tests that covered it before the port was shared. A second server has not been connected to a real Discord server.

A reminder or any other deferred turn set BY VOICE still arrives as a text message, deliberately: speaking unprompted into a voice channel is a much larger claim than answering a question just asked in one.

Two test suites under `deploy/` have never run in the main gate, which is limited to `tests/`. Found because one of them still asserted a field deleted earlier the same day — a rename that should have reddened it and could not. Not fixed here; those suites are run by hand and by the container builds.

Supersedes three earlier unreleased fragments' claims about how voice is configured: the wake gate and the audio-controller no longer take ANY server or channel id from the environment, and the transcript POST carries a server id rather than a conversation id. Where those fragments say otherwise, this one is current.
reason: Supersedes and replaces the unreleased 'one-audio-controller-per-guild' fragment, which described an intermediate shape that never reached a deployment: a second container per guild behind a compose profile, needing VOICE_GUILD_ID_B in .env. The operator rejected that third copy of the guild id, and the containers turned out to be unnecessary — each guild's audio stack was already built by a per-guild factory, and what actually blocked sharing one process was the HTTP port and the audio seam. design/voice-channel/07 §12.5 stands unchanged throughout.
